features.name: counter_quote_mark_count
features.definition: How many quotation mark characters appear across all counter-argument comments?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments with json.loads into a list of strings. If missing, unparseable or not a list, return null. If the list is empty return 0. Otherwise return the sum over all comments (non-string entries skipped) of the number of characters in the set: straight double quote ", curly double quotes “ and ”. Single quotes/apostrophes and '>' blockquote markers are not counted. Pure raw character count, no semantic filtering of who is quoted or whether the quote is adopted.

h0: counter_quote_mark_count has no association with the probability that the OP changed their view (delta).
h1: Higher counter_quote_mark_count is associated with a lower probability that the OP changed their view (delta).
note: Operational assumptions: "more quotation marks" is measured as total count of double-quotation-mark characters across all available counter-argument comments (not normalized by length, so it is correlated with total comment length/number of comments; no control is added). Quotation marks also mark scare quotes, titles or the OP's own words, not only quoting others; the raw count does not verify quoted speaker. Blockquote markers not counted. "Persuasive" is operationalized only as the dataset outcome delta (OP view change); association only, not causal. Comments may include text after outcome/delta announcements; the raw count is not outcome-free and comment timing is unknown.
